result.notes: All 9 gates implemented as tests; full suite 318 passed (no failures I did not cause — none at all). Method followed exactly (cyclic de Bruijn, field FFT filtering, square-law detect, exhaustive phase/eye search, flat-loss normalized out with IL reported separately and a double-count warning; driven-ring-modulator exclusion stated in the docstring). Physics findings baked into tests honestly: (a) sampling the analytic H on a finite FFT band leaves a tiny band-edge truncation residual (~ +/-0.006 dB for a 50x-baud pole), so the wideband-limit gate asserts |penalty| < 0.02 dB and gate 7 uses samples_per_symbol=32 where the 8 GBd ring penalty is genuinely >= 0 (+0.002 dB, converging to +0.003 at sps=64); (b) gate 6 uses a Gaussian low-pass on a 4M-point grid so the effective discrete filter is FFT-length-independent — random-vs-de-Bruijn diffs land at ~1e-11, safely inside the +1e-9 tolerance (a single-pole filter fails this gate at ~5e-4 dB because its sinc-truncation tails alias differently for N=4096 vs N=8192 symbols); (c) 4 dB ER penalty measured slightly BELOW the infinite-ER penalty for the 0.7x-baud pole (0.1162 vs 0.1166 dB), so the test asserts finite/positive/close, not a sign. Example 07 runs (exit 0): composed 4-ring 200-GHz demux drop1 (FWHM ~41 GHz, IL 0.166 dB) gives NRZ penalties -0.001/0.001/0.174/0.938 dB at 8/16/32/53.125 GBd; CPO preset margin +14.95 -> +14.78 dB (delta -0.174 dB). matplotlib absent in venv, plot skipped gracefully per the 03/06 pattern. Only the three assigned files were created; __init__.py untouched (from siphon import isi works as a submodule import).

result.checks_run: Read src/siphon/isi.py, tests/test_isi.py, examples/07_filter_isi.py, src/siphon/link.py (LinkBudget, presets). Ran full test suite (uv run pytest tests/test_isi.py: 29 passed). Ran examples/07_filter_isi.py end to end and recomputed its margin delta by hand (delta = upgraded.margin - base.margin = -sum-of-added-penalties = -0.174 dB; matches printed output exactly). Wrote /tmp scratch scripts (repo untouched): (1) pure-delay sweep tau = 0.3/0.999/1.0/1.3/2.0/3.0 UI through filter_isi_penalty_db; (2) analytic two-tap field-echo cross-check H(f)=(1+0.1 e^{-2pi i f T})/1.1 -> module 0.871502 dB vs closed-form 10log10((1+a)^2/(1-a^2)) = 0.871502 dB (verifies FFT baseband mapping, delay sign convention vs exp(-i 2pi neff L/wl), square-law detection, and 10log10 optical-power penalty scale); (3) NaN-in-s21 probe. Verified fftfreq bin-0 = carrier, no-extrapolation guard, monotonicity/shape/parameter validation paths, ER handling (inf and finite), de Bruijn property tests, and that preset_cpo_optical_io's path contains no demux loss element.

findings.claim: The docstring claims "clock recovery absorbs group delay", but the sampling-phase search only spans [0, 1) UI: any S21 with bulk group delay >= ~1 UI is silently reported as penalty_db = inf ("eye closed") when the true ISI penalty is ~0 dB. The per-slot samples are grouped against the unshifted transmitted symbol sequence in _best_eye (samples[symbols == j]), so an integer-UI delay mislabels every sample's level and the sub-eye openings go negative.
findings.evidence: Numeric repro (/tmp/isi_delay_repro.py, 32 GBd NRZ, sps=20, pure delay H(f)=exp(-2j*pi*f*tau)): tau=0.3 UI -> penalty 2.8e-11 dB (correct), but tau=0.999, 1.0, 1.3, 2.0, 3.0 UI -> penalty = inf with IL = 0.000 dB in every case. inf is indistinguishable from a genuinely closed eye (same value TestClosedEye pins), so the garbage is silent. Plausible use per the module's own intended flow ("a filter cascade from siphon.circuit.Circuit"): 1 UI at 53.125 GBd is 18.8 ps, i.e. ~1.3 mm of silicon routing at ng=4.2, and any composed circuit containing mm-scale bus/access waveguides or a fiber jumper exceeds it. tests/test_isi.py TestPureDelay only exercises tau=0.3 UI, so the >=1 UI regime is unpinned.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the linear-phase (bulk delay) component of H before filtering — e.g. estimate integer-UI delay from the phase slope d(arg H)/df or from the peak of the cross-correlation of intensity with the pattern, and cyclically roll the symbol labels by that integer before _best_eye; or search integer symbol offsets alongside the sampling phase. At minimum, narrow the docstring claim to "sub-UI group delay" and raise/warn when the estimated delay exceeds 1 UI. Add a >=1 UI delay test.

findings.claim: The double-count WARNING's premise — "that insertion loss is already carried in the link path budget (couplers, demux loss elements)" — is false for the shipped preset the flow is demonstrated on: preset_cpo_optical_io()'s path (link.py lines 730-737) contains couplers and routing but NO demux/filter loss element, so following the documented flow (example 07 lines 226-231) books the drop-port IL nowhere and the "upgraded" margin is optimistic by exactly that IL.
findings.evidence: Ran examples/07_filter_isi.py: result_32.insertion_loss_db = 0.166 dB; upgraded budget adds only penalties_db['demux_isi']=0.174 and prints MARGIN +14.78 dB. A budget that also books the 0.166 dB drop IL in the path would read +14.61 dB. The example prints a note that the IL "belongs in the PATH as a LossElement" (line 235-237) but never adds it, and the headline margin-delta sentence (line 233) presents the upgrade as complete. With a lossier/detuned demux (e.g. higher loss_db_per_cm or carrier off-peak) the uncharged IL is dB-scale, not 0.17 dB.
findings.suggested_fix: In example 07, actually book the IL: upgraded = replace(base, path=base.path + [LossElement('demux drop IL', result_32.insertion_loss_db)], penalties_db={..., 'demux_isi': ...}), and report the combined delta. In isi.py, soften the warning to "is normally carried ... — verify your path actually contains a demux/filter loss element before dropping it".

findings.claim: The example docstring claims the computed ISI penalty "replaces a hand-entered placeholder in the link budget", but preset_cpo_optical_io() has no ISI/demux placeholder to replace — its penalties_db is {'wdm_crosstalk': 0.3, 'wavelength_drift': 0.5} (link.py lines 745-748) — so the code (line 227-230) ADDS a new 'demux_isi' entry and the margin strictly decreases; nothing hand-entered is superseded.
findings.evidence: Exact-line contradiction: examples/07_filter_isi.py line 7 ("penalty replaces a hand-entered placeholder in the link budget") vs src/siphon/link.py lines 745-748 (penalties_db has no ISI entry; the DR4 preset's 'isi_equalization': 1.0 at line 704 is the only hand-entered ISI allocation, and it is in the other preset). Runtime waterfall confirms: 'penalty: demux_isi +0.17 dB' appears as a third row alongside the two preset rows, margin +14.95 -> +14.78.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the docstring to "adds a computed penalties_db['demux_isi'] entry that would otherwise be a hand-entered allocation (cf. the DR4 preset's 'isi_equalization')", or demonstrate an actual replacement by starting from a budget containing a placeholder ISI entry.

findings.claim: A NaN anywhere in s21 within the simulation band silently yields IsiResult(penalty_db=nan, insertion_loss_db=nan) instead of raising — the only degenerate-carrier guard is abs(h0) == 0.0, which NaN passes — so the NaN propagates into LinkBudget.penalties_db and margin_db as a silent NaN, contradicting the module's otherwise raise-on-bad-input contract (closed eye -> inf, null -> ValueError, span/monotonic/shape -> ValueError).
findings.evidence: Numeric repro (/tmp/isi_xcheck.py): wl=linspace(1.50,1.60,101), s21=ones except s21[50]=nan at the carrier -> filter_isi_penalty_db returns penalty_db = nan, insertion_loss_db = nan, and report() prints "ISI penalty (beyond flat loss) : nan dB" with no exception. In _best_eye the NaN makes worst = nan, so the `worst <= 0.0` closed-eye branch is False and math.log10 propagates nan. tests/test_isi.py has no non-finite-input test.
findings.suggested_fix: After building t21 (or h), raise ValueError if not np.all(np.isfinite(t21)) ("s21 contains non-finite values"); one line next to the existing shape check at isi.py line 294.

result.checks_run: Read src/siphon/isi.py, tests/test_isi.py, examples/07_filter_isi.py, and convention sources (components.py Straight/RingAddDrop docstrings, module convention header). Ran the full ISI test suite (29 passed). Built independent numeric checks in /tmp with the project venv: (1) delay-sign check — impulse through a Straight of 3-sample group delay peaks at +3 samples, confirming exp(-1j*2*pi*neff*L/wl) + numpy fftfreq/ifft maps positive group delay to a positive baseband delay; (2) analytic one-symbol echo H(f)=1+0.2*exp(-2j*pi*f*T): module reproduces closed-form penalty 1.760913 dB and IL 1.583625 dB to 1e-6, validating field cross-terms, |H(fc)|^2 normalization, eye construction and penalty definition; (3) flat-delay invariance sweep on a single-pole filter (0/0.3/0.6/0.8/0.95 UI added delay); (4) pure-delay Straights at 0.9 and 1.5 UI; (5) ring add-drop demux preceded by 0/0.5/1/2/5 mm routing Straights at 32 GBd; (6) example 07's composed 4-ring demux at all four shipped bauds, comparing as-shipped vs carrier-group-delay-removed penalties (benign, <=0.06 dB); (7) wavelength-grid density sweep for a 670 um Straight. Repo untouched; all scripts under /tmp.

findings.claim: The eye search never compensates whole-symbol group delay: samples are grouped by transmitted symbol at the same row index and the phase search spans only [0,1) UI, so any composed response whose aggregate group delay pushes the eye center past ~1 UI (routing waveguides, long paths) returns a grossly inflated or infinite penalty for a physically delay-invariant quantity, directly contradicting the docstring claim at line 61 that 'clock recovery absorbs group delay'.
findings.evidence: Numeric reproductions (project venv, /tmp scripts): (a) a bare Straight with 1.5 UI group delay (L=3346 um, ng=4.2, 32 GBd) returns penalty_db=inf; physical answer is 0 (a pure delay closes nothing), and the module's own TestPureDelay proves 0.3 UI gives ~0. (b) Single-pole 0.7x-baud filter: penalty 0.117 dB alone, but multiplying by a flat exp(-2j*pi*f*tau) delay gives 0.509 dB (tau=0.3 UI), 2.165 dB (0.6 UI), 13.812 dB (0.8 UI), inf (0.95 UI and 5 UI) — the reported sampling phase saturates at 15/16 UI, showing the search hitting the row boundary. (c) Plausible use per the module's stated scope ('demuxes, couplers, and other passives the signal traverses'): the test-suite's RingAddDrop demux preceded by an ordinary routing Straight at 32 GBd gives penalty 1.494 dB (0 um route) -> 2.621 dB (500 um, 0.22 UI) -> 5.234 dB (1 mm, 0.45 UI) -> inf (2 mm, 0.90 UI). The shipped example 07 stays benign only because its composed delay is <=0.42 UI (as-shipped vs delay-removed penalties differ <=0.06 dB). Everything else validates exactly: delay sign convention confirmed (impulse through a 3-sample-delay Straight shifts +3 samples), and an analytic one-symbol echo H=1+0.2exp(-2j*pi*f*T) reproduces penalty 1.760913 dB and IL 1.583625 dB to 1e-6.
findings.suggested_fix: Before _best_eye, remove the integer-sample bulk delay: estimate tau_g from the phase slope of h around bin 0 (or argmax of circular cross-correlation between detected intensity and the ideal pattern) and np.roll(intensity, -round(tau_g*fs)); the existing sub-UI phase search then absorbs the remainder, making the result delay-invariant as documented. Add a regression test with a >=1 UI pure delay and with a ring+routing-Straight composition (TestPureDelay's 0.3 UI is below the failure threshold).

findings.claim: _baseband_response validates only the wavelength span, not the grid density; linear interpolation of real/imag parts of a rapidly rotating S21 phasor (any path with appreciable physical length) silently attenuates/distorts the response and fabricates penalty, with no warning or documented sampling requirement.
findings.evidence: A 670 um Straight (0.3 UI delay at 32 GBd, penalty should be ~0 and is 7e-10 dB on a 2M-point grid) yields spurious penalty 0.0009 dB at 2001 points, 0.0139 dB at 501 points, and 0.0782 dB at 201 points over a 10 nm span — all grids that pass the span check without complaint. Error grows with path length (phase slope 2*pi*ng*L/wl^2 per grid step), so coarse user grids on composed circuits with routing produce quietly wrong numbers.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the maximum bin-to-bin phase step of the interpolated h (or of s21 across adjacent grid points within the band) and raise/warn when it exceeds ~0.5 rad, stating the required grid density; or interpolate in magnitude/unwrapped-phase instead of real/imag. Document the density requirement next to the span requirement in the docstring.

result.checks_run: Read src/siphon/isi.py, tests/test_isi.py, examples/07_filter_isi.py plus neighbors (components.py RingAddDrop/Straight, circuit.py). Numeric attacks run as /tmp scratch scripts against the installed package (repo untouched): (1) de Bruijn cyclic exhaustiveness independently re-verified for (2,4), (3,3), (2,16), (4,8) — all k**n windows distinct; (2) FFT-bin interpolation / fftfreq ordering / Nyquist bin cross-checked against a 512x-oversampled exact ZOH time-domain single-pole reference (reference 0.1091 dB, engine 0.1166 dB at sps=16, 0.1115 dB at sps=64 — converging, no off-by-one) and fractional pure-delay reproduction to 6e-9 dB; (3) group-delay handling probed with pure delays 0.3/0.9/1.0/1.3/2.5 UI and with test-7's kappa^2=0.05 ring plus 1/3/5 mm Straight-equivalent waveguide phase, compared against a delay-agnostic reference (same engine, eye search allowed integer-UI symbol rolls); (4) memory_symbols truncation swept mem=6/7/10/14 for kappa^2=0.05/0.02/0.01 rings at 32 GBd (kappa 0.05 converges to 0.0006 dB between mem 6 and 7; kappa 0.01 eye is genuinely closed per the delay-agnostic reference, so gate 7's 0.15 dB tolerance hides nothing); (5) example 07's composed 4-ring demux re-simulated at all four bauds and compared to the delay-agnostic reference — identical (roll 0), example output unaffected; (6) closed-eye inf path, ER handling, normalization, and test gate float tolerances inspected.

findings.claim: The eye search absorbs only the fractional part of the path group delay: _best_eye groups the detected sample in symbol slot i by transmitted symbol i and searches sampling phases only within one UI, so any response whose optimal sampling instant crosses a symbol boundary (total group delay of order 1 UI or more) has its samples labeled with the wrong symbols, producing a grossly inflated penalty or a spurious 'eye closed' (inf) for physically benign delay. This contradicts the module docstring's exact claim at line 61, '(clock recovery absorbs group delay)', and the 'exhaustive' claim: real clock recovery absorbs integer-UI delay too.
findings.evidence: Numeric reproductions (scratch scripts in /tmp/isi_review, run against the installed package): (a) a pure delay H(f)=exp(-2j*pi*f*tau) — zero true ISI — gives penalty 6e-9 dB at tau=0.3 UI and 6e-8 dB at 0.9 UI, but penalty = inf at tau = 1.0, 1.3, and 2.5 UI; (b) the exact ring blessed by tests/test_isi.py TestRingDropPort (kappa^2=0.05, 32 GBd, true penalty 1.49 dB, its own best phase already 0.969 UI) composed with a 1 mm routing waveguide phase exp(-2j*pi*neff*L/wl) (0.45 UI group delay at ng=4.2, the library's Straight component transfer) reports 5.24 dB where a delay-agnostic reference (identical engine, eye search additionally allowed integer-UI rolls of the symbol labels) gives 1.51 dB; with 3 mm (1.34 UI) it reports inf vs true 1.50 dB. Straight (components.py line 79) is a first-class circuit element carrying full propagation phase, and filter_isi_penalty_db's documented intended input is circuit.transmission of composed circuits, so a few mm of on-chip routing at 32+ GBd silently corrupts the budgeted penalty. Example 07 happens to be unaffected only because its demux contains no Straight segments and ring delay stays below ~0.5 UI (verified: reported equals delay-agnostic at all four bauds). tests/test_isi.py TestPureDelay only exercises tau=0.3 UI, so the regime is untested.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the integer (or full linear) part of the group delay before the eye search: estimate tau_g from the phase slope of h around bin 0 (e.g., tau_g = -dphase/d(2*pi*f) via the first FFT bins, or a weighted least-squares over the signal band), multiply h by exp(+2j*pi*f_hz*round(tau_g*rate)*T) to fold the integer-UI part out, and keep the existing fractional-phase search; alternatively extend _best_eye to also search integer cyclic rolls of the symbol labels (np.roll(symbols, k) for k in a small range set by the estimated group delay) and report the combined phase as sampling_phase_ui possibly >= 1 UI. Add a pure-delay test at tau >= 1 UI asserting ~0 dB penalty.
